title: Helium-Gas-Cooled Cryogenic Current Comparator Integrated with a Quantum Resistance Standard
authors: Yuma Okazaki, Takehiko Oe, Nobu-Hisa Kaneko
abstract: We report a cryogen-free cryogenic current comparator (CCC) system for precision resistance measurements. A helium-gas chamber was developed and installed on the 4 K stage of a cryogen-free dilution refrigerator equipped with a pulse-tube cryocooler. The CCC probe was housed in this chamber and was cooled through helium gas serving as a heat exchange medium. The metrological performance of this helium-gas-cooled CCC was evaluated through precision resistance-ratio measurements and found to be comparable to that obtained under liquid-helium cooling. A quantum Hall resistance (QHR) device was also integrated into the same refrigerator, enabling QHR/100~$Ω$ resistance-ratio measurements. The type-A uncertainty reached the 1~n$Ω$/$Ω$ level within an averaging time of 100~s, and the resulting resistance-ratio measurements agreed well with conventional liquid-helium-based measurements at the level of a few n$Ω$/$Ω$. The system provides this level of measurement performance while consuming less than 1~L of helium gas per thermal cycle.
summary: This paper reports the successful development of a cryogenic current comparator (CCC) that operates using helium gas instead of liquid helium. The system maintains high measurement precision, comparable to liquid-helium standards, and is successfully integrated with a Quantum Hall Resistance standard. This advancement significantly improves the practicality and sustainability of high-precision resistance metrology.
main_problem: The primary goal was to develop and validate a high-precision cryogenic current comparator (CCC) system that operates without relying on liquid helium, thereby reducing operational costs and logistical constraints.
main_result: The helium-gas-cooled CCC achieved metrological performance comparable to liquid-helium cooling, successfully integrating with a Quantum Hall Resistance (QHR) standard with uncertainties reaching the nΩ/Ω level.
method: The authors utilized a custom helium-gas chamber cooled by a cryogen-free dilution refrigerator to cool the CCC probe, allowing for precision resistance-ratio measurements.
model_or_system: The system involves a CCC probe and a QHR standard integrated into a dilution refrigerator. Cooling is achieved via a helium gas medium in a custom chamber, which is thermally anchored to the 4 K stage.
key_observables: Type-A uncertainty ($1 	ext{ n}\Omega/\Omega$), SQUID $\phi-V$ characteristics, resistance-ratio measurements, and stage temperatures.
important_parameters: Operating temperature (4 K stage), helium gas pressure (low-pressure regime), and measurement time (e.g., 100 s averaging time).
main_assumptions: The performance is assumed to be comparable to liquid-helium cooling, and thermal anchoring is crucial for minimizing heat load.
figures_summary: Figures detail the physical setup, including the gas chamber and thermal anchors. Other figures show the dependence of SQUID amplitude and stage temperatures on helium gas pressure, and plots of resistance ratios and Allan deviations over time.
paper_structure: The paper details the engineering challenges of cryogen-free operation, presents the methodology for cooling the CCC with helium gas, validates the performance against liquid helium standards, and finally demonstrates the integration with a QHR standard.
why_interesting: While the core physics is metrology, the engineering challenge of maintaining ultra-low noise, stable cryogenic environments using non-traditional cooling media (helium gas) is highly relevant to building complex quantum measurement apparatuses.
